sections.h2: Contacting the Edgecombe County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Land records sit here beside births, deaths, marriages, military discharges, notary files and maps. The office phone is (252) 641-7924, and that is the number to use for counter hours and the street address. Tarboro is the county seat.

Once you sign a deed to sell an Edgecombe County house, it is filed in this office, normally by your closing attorney. What follows explains the charges and the local habits that can hold up a recording.

A deed is recorded as a general document: $26.00 buys the first 15 pages, and every extra page adds $4.00. The excise tax is a separate $1.00 for each $500.00.

Edgecombe County register of deeds fees
ServiceFee
General instruments (not deeds of trust or mortgages)$26.00 first 15 pages; $4.00 per page past 15
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 first 35 pages; $4.00 per page past 35
Excise tax$1.00 per $500.00
Nonstandard document$25.00 plus the recording fee
Plat$21.00
Certified copy$5.00 page one, $2.00 per later page
Plain copy$.10 a page
Map copy$.50 at 11 x 17, $1.00 at 18 x 24
Satisfaction of a mortgageNo fee

Staff process filings and requests the same day they arrive. People filing by post should put a stamped return envelope, addressed to themselves, in with the papers.

Under a county resolution, no deed is recorded until the Tax Collector has certified it, unless there is a workaround. The workaround is a line on the deed saying that a North Carolina attorney drew it up and that the closing attorney will send any overdue taxes to the tax collector out of the sale money.

Your attorney can put that line in. Anyone who writes a deed without an attorney must visit the Tax Collector and request the certification first.

  • Attorney route: the preparer statement satisfies the resolution, and back taxes come out of your proceeds.
  • Do it yourself route: obtain the certification before bringing the deed to the register.

sections.h2: Can a deed be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. Simplifile is the vendor on the county's E-Recording page, which also points to CSC eRecording Solutions. A firm or title agent holding an account can transmit a deed with no courier.

If you have no account, your closing attorney can file it for you. Paper filings follow the state filing standards, which the Real Estate page posts as a PDF beside an Assumed Name form and property check instructions.

sections.h2: What must never appear in a recorded document
sections.html:
Leave out Social Security, taxpayer ID, driver's license, state ID, passport, bank account, credit card and debit card numbers, plus PINs and passwords. G.S. 132-1.10(g)(1) allows a number like that only if a law or court order requires it or if just the last four digits are shown.

Filed documents join the official county records, so read yours before signing and ask the preparer to strip anything sensitive.

The recording date counts as the transfer date for Present Use Value. To keep farm or forest land in the program, the buyer files a new application within 60 days of that date.

Deferred taxes, even from years before your sale, pass to the new owner. When land drops out of the program, the current year and three earlier years are due with interest. If you own land like this, call the Tax Assessor about its status before you list or entertain an offer.

  • Farm use needs 10 cultivated acres, and forest use needs 20 forested acres plus a management plan.
  • Farm income must average $1000 a year across the last three years.
  • A sale to an owner who cannot qualify can take the land out of the program.

A certified birth, death or marriage certificate is $10 a copy. You can order online through Permitium/AIS, which tacks on a $3.35 convenience fee and card fees, or mail in an application. Birth and death files start in October 1913, and marriage files start in 1867.

Heirs selling an inherited house usually need a certified death certificate for the estate paperwork. Order it early so it is in hand when the buyer's attorney asks.

sections.h2: How property taxes connect to the deed
sections.html:
Real estate, personal property and vehicle tax for the county, 14 fire districts, one drainage district and eight towns all flow through the Tax Collector. That office writes the statements of taxes due that attorneys and agents ask for, so have your closing attorney request one ahead of the closing date.

Call (252) 641-7810 about taxes paid or owed, and the Tax Assessor at (252) 641-7855 about a value. Our Edgecombe County property tax guide covers rates, listing and appeals.

sections.h2: Rocky Mount and Tarboro homes: which county office?
sections.html:
The land decides the county. A house in Tarboro belongs in the Edgecombe County office, and so does anything on the Edgecombe side of Rocky Mount. Because Rocky Mount straddles Nash and Edgecombe counties and is the largest municipality here, find out which side your parcel is on before the deed goes out.

A single parcel that crosses the line pays its excise tax to whichever county holds the larger share of the value. A parcel in one of the small towns, such as Princeville, Pinetops, Whitakers, Speed, Leggett, Conetoe, Macclesfield or Sharpsburg, still needs its county confirmed.

Before the signing appointment, have your attorney verify the parcel number and county. Same day processing helps only if the paper lands at the right office.

1. Ask the Tax Collector for a statement of what is owed on the parcel.
  2. Let the attorney draft the deed with either the preparer statement or a certification in hand.
  3. Settle the excise tax at filing. You owe it as seller, and the register takes it with the deed.
  4. Send the deed in electronically if your attorney or title agent has an account.
  5. Expect any mortgage payoff to produce a satisfaction that costs nothing to record.

Plan on a short wait only if everything arrives together. Bring or send the signed deed, the payment for recording and the excise tax, and the tax certification or preparer statement. A missing piece sends the packet back, and mailed packets lose days in the post. Phone (252) 641-7924 if you are unsure what your attorney has already handled.

Selling for cash removes the lender's paperwork. The deed, the excise tax and the tax certification stay exactly the same.

The county counts 49,121 residents (July 2025 estimate) and 23,604 housing units. Owners occupy 60.8% of homes, and the median value is $125,100. Page charges are the same for a modest house as for an expensive one. Only the excise tax rises with the price, so it is usually the largest recording cost.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a mortgage release in Edgecombe County?
faqs.a: No. The office records a satisfaction for free, so a mortgage release at closing costs nothing to file.

faqs.q: What is the Edgecombe County excise tax rate?
faqs.a: It is $1.00 per $500.00. As the seller you pay it to the register of deeds when the deed is filed.

faqs.q: Does Edgecombe County record a deed that lacks a tax certification?
faqs.a: Only if the deed carries the attorney preparer statement. Otherwise the Tax Collector must certify it. The statement must say a North Carolina attorney prepared the deed and the closing attorney will pay delinquent taxes from proceeds.

faqs.q: How do I get a certified birth or death certificate in Edgecombe County?
faqs.a: Either order through Permitium/AIS or mail in the application. A copy is $10, and ordering online also costs a $3.35 convenience fee plus card fees.

faqs.q: Does the Edgecombe County register accept electronic filing?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile, with CSC eRecording Solutions as another option. Your attorney or title agent normally does the submitting.
